Available at extractivism.online as a web-native work.", "title": "New Extractivism", "year": "2020"}, {"description": "Collaboration with Kate Crawford (AI Now Institute, NYU). name: Mario Klingemann
metadata: {"active_years": "2015-present (generative/AI art; earlier digital art from ~2000s; net art from ~1998)", "canon_tier": "primary", "collaborators": [{"name": "Memo Akten", "type": "COLLABORATES_WITH"}], "data_provenance": {"confidence": "high", "source": "seed-research-2025", "trust_tier": "reviewed"}, "exhibitions": ["Sotheby's", "Ars Electronica", "ZKM", "Onassis Stegi", "Centre Pompidou-Metz"], "image_license": null, "image_source": null, "image_url": null, "key_works": [{"description": "Autonomous GAN-based painting machine that continuously generates new 'portraits' of people who never existed, displayed on two period-styled picture-framed screens driven by a custom-built AI system. The piece was sold at Sotheby's in 2019 — one of the earliest autonomous-AI works to enter the major auction circuit — and is a reference work for the argument that an AI system can be the author of a perpetually-new artwork. Its slowness and refusal to cache images makes the non-reproducibility of its outputs part of the content.", "title": "Memories of Passersby I", "year": "2018"}, {"description": "Series of GAN-portraits produced by deliberately damaging the trained models — truncating weights, feeding noise, perturbing latent vectors — to elicit eerie, melted, unstable faces. The series argued that AI image-making's aesthetic heart was in the breakdowns and edge-cases, not the clean outputs, and it shaped the first generation of AI-art visual vocabulary substantially before the diffusion-model era.", "title": "Neural Glitch series", "year": "2017-2019"}, {"description": "Decentralised-autonomous-artist project for which Klingemann serves as primary artistic director and technical lead. Botto generates candidate images weekly; a DAO of token-holders votes on which to mint. The project is an explicit test of whether AI-generated art can be collectively authored, and it is one of the most widely-watched current experiments in AI-DAO governance of aesthetic decisions.", "title": "Botto (artistic direction)", "year": "2021-present"}], "location": null, "medium": ["GAN", "diffusion", "generative software", "installation", "print"], "merged_from": ["practitioner:mario klingemann quasimondo"], "original_type": "artist", "scene_affiliation": ["AI art", "creative coding"], "seed_category": null, "source_file": "stub-promoted", "source_origin": "ai_assisted", "status": "confirmed", "sub_type": "artist", "url": "https://quasimondo.com/", "wikidata_qid": null}

Shulgin treats the form as the overlooked aesthetic substrate of the administered web, and Form Art competitions (1997) invited peers to submit works made only of these ostensibly utilitarian elements. The piece argues that bureaucratic UI is already expressive, and that net.art can locate its medium in the browser's structural vocabulary rather than in image or video.", "title": "Form Art", "year": "1997"}, {"description": "Long-running cybernetic-punk performance project in which an obsolete 386DX PC equipped with Microsoft SAM text-to-speech covers rock and punk songs live. The obsolete machine as performance instrument stages computational obsolescence as continuing labour rather than disposal; the covers' flat, affectless speech foregrounds the gap between machine-reproduced and live performance. The work has toured internationally for over two decades, treating a single ageing computer as durational co-performer.", "title": "386DX", "year": "1998-present"}, {"description": "Early web-native work diagnosing informational overload as a somatic condition, predating most discourse on digital burnout by a decade.
